(std::abs(det) < EPSILON) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n427: \n428:     val_t invDet = 1.0f / det;\n429:     Vec3 tvec = orig - v0;\n430:     val_t u = tvec.dot(pvec) * invDet;\n431:     if (u < 0.0f || u > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n432: \n433:     Vec3 qvec = tvec.cross(e1);\n434:     val_t v = dir.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n435:     if (v < 0.0f || u + v > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n436: \n437:     return e2.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n438: }\n439: \n440: // ============================================================================\n441: // Visibility Testing (Octree-accelerated)\n442: // ============================================================================\n443: \n444: // Check if a ray between two triangles is blocked by any \n454:     return octree.applyToTris(from, to, [&](size_t idx, const Triangle& tri) {\n455:         if (idx == srcTriIdx || idx == dstTriIdx) return false;\n456: \n457:         val_t dist = rayTriangleIntersect(from, dirNorm, tri.a, tri.b, tri.c);\n458:         if (dist > EPSILON && dist < rayLen - EPSILON) {\n459:             return true;  // Ray is blocked\n460:         }\n461: ============================================================================\n468: \n469: // Compute the cosine of angle between vector and triangle normal\n470: val_t cosPhi(const Vec3& v, const Vec3& normal) {\n471:     val_t vNorm = v.norm();\n472:     if (vNorm <= EPSILON) return ZERO;\n473:     return std::max(ZERO, v.dot(normal) / vNorm);\n474: }\n475: \n476: // Compute form factor Kij Octree& octree,\n480:                   RandomGenerator& rng) {\n481:     const Triangle& triI = triangles[idxI];\n482:     const Triangle& triJ = triangles[idxJ];\n483: \n484:     // Cull triangles facing the same direction\n485:     if (triI.normal().dot(triJ.normal()) > 0.99f) return ZERO;\n486: \n487:     val_t kij = ZERO;\n488: \n489:     for (int r = 0; r < NUM_RAYS; ++r) {\n490:         Vec3 pI = randomPointInTriangle(triI, rng);\n491:         Vec3 pJ = randomPointInTriangle(triJ, rng);\n492: \n493:         if (isRayBlocked(pI, pJ, octree, idxI, idxJ)) continue;\n494: \n495:         Vec3 v = pJ - pI;\n496:         val_t distSqr = v.squaredNorm();\n497:         if (distSqr < EPSILON) continue;\n498: \n499:         val_t cosPhiI = cosPhi(v, triI.normal());\n500:         val_t cosPhiJ = cosPhi(-v, triJ.normal());\n501: \n502:         if (cosPhiI <= ZERO || cosPhiJ <= ZERO) continue;\n503: \n504:         kij += (cosPhiI * cosPhiJ) / (PI * distSqr);\n505:     }\n506: \n507: Vec3 {\n    val_t x, y, z;\n\n    constexpr Vec3() : x(0), y(0), z(0) {}\n    constexpr Vec3(val_t x, val_t y, val_t z) : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n    explicit constexpr Vec3(val_t v) : x(v), y(v), z(v) const { return {x * s, y * s, z * s}; }\n    Vec3 operator/(val_t s) const { return {x / s, y / s, z / s}; }\n    Vec3 operator-() const { return {-x, -y, -z}; }\n\n    val_t dot(const Vec3& o) const { return x * o.x + y * o.y + z * o.z; }\n    Vec3 cross(const Vec3& o) const {\n        return {y * o.z - z * o.y, z * o.x - x * o.z, x * o.y - y * o.x};\n    }\n\n    val_t squaredNorm() const { ============================================================================\n// Triangle-Box Overlap Test (for octree construction)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Separating axis test for triangle-box overlap\nbool triangleBoxOverlap(const Vec3& boxCenter, const Vec3& boxHalfSize, const Triangle& tri) {\n    // Translate triangle to box center\n    Vec3 v0 = tri.a - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v1 = tri.b - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v2 = tri.c - boxCenter;\n\n    // Triangle edges\n    Vec3 e0 = v1 - v0;\n    Vec3 e1 = v2 - v1;\n    Vec3 e2 = v0 - v2;\n\n    // Test box normals (AABB axes)\n    auto minMax3 = [](val_t a, val_t b, val_t c) {\n        return std::make_pair(std::min({a, b, c}), std::max({a, b, c}));\n    };\n\n    auto [minX, maxX] = minMax3(v0.x, v1.x, v2.x);\n    if (minX > boxHalfSize.x || maxX < -boxHalfSize.x) return false;\n\n    auto [minY, maxY] = minMax3(v0.y, v1.y, v2.y);\n    if (minY > boxHalfSize.y || maxY < -boxHalfSize.y) return false;\n\n    auto [minZ, maxZ] = minMax3(v0.z, v1.z, v2.z);\n    if (minZ > boxHalfSize.z || maxZ < -boxHalfSize.z) return false;\n\n    // Test triangle normal\n    Vec3 triNormal = e0.cross(e1);\n    val_t d = triNormal.dot(v0);\n    val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(triNormal.x) +\n              boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(triNormal.y) +\n              boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(triNormal.z);\n    if (std::abs(d) > r) return false;\n\n    // Test 9 edge cross products\n    auto testAxis = [&](const Vec3& axis) {\n        val_t p0 = axis.dot(v0);\n        val_t p1 = axis.dot(v1);\n        val_t p2 = axis.dot(v2);\n        val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(axis.x) +\n                  boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(axis.y) +\n                  boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(axis.z);\n        auto [minP, maxP] = minMax3(p0, p1, p2);\n        return !(minP > r || maxP < -r);\n    };\n\n    Vec3 axes[3] = {{1,0,0}, {0,1,0}, {0,0,1}};\n    Vec3 edges[3] = {e0, e1, e2};\n    for (const auto& axis : axes) {\n        for (const auto& edge : edges) {\n            Vec3 crossAxis = axis.cross(edge);\n            if (crossAxis.squaredNorm() > EPSILON) {\n                if (!testAxis(crossAxis)) return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Octree for Spatial Acceleration\n// ============================================================================\n\nconstexpr size_t MAX_OCTREE_TRIS = 8;\nconstexpr val_t MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE = 0.5f;\n\nclass Octree {\npublic:\n    Vec3 minBound, maxBound;\n    Vec3 halfExtent, center;\n    std::unique_ptr<Octree> children[8];\n    std::vector<size_t> triangleIndices;  // Indices into the global triangle list\n    const std::vector<Triangle>* allTriangles;  // Pointer to all triangles\n\n    Octree() : allTriangles(nullptr) {}\n\n    void build(const std::vector<Triangle>& triangles) {\n        allTriangles = &triangles;\n        if (triangles.empty()) return;\n\n        // Compute bounding box\n        minBound = triangles[0].a;\n        maxBound = triangles[0].a;\n        for (const auto& tri : triangles) {\n            for (const auto* v : {&tri.a, &tri.b, &tri.c}) {\n                minBound.x = std::min(minBound.x, v->x);\n                minBound.y = std::min(minBound.y, v->y);\n                minBound.z = std::min(minBound.z, v->z);\n                maxBound.x = std::max(maxBound.x, v->x);\n                maxBound.y = std::max(maxBound.y, v->y);\n                maxBound.z = std::max(maxBound.z, v->z);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Collect all indices\n        std::vector<size_t> allIndices(triangles.size());\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < triangles.size(); ++i) allIndices[i] = i;\n\n        buildNode(allIndices, minBound, maxBound);\n    }\n\nprivate:\n    void buildNode(const std::vector<size_t>& indices, const Vec3& nodeMin, const Vec3& nodeMax) {\n        minBound = nodeMin;\n        maxBound = nodeMax;\n        halfExtent = (maxBound - minBound) * 0.5f;\n        center = (minBound + maxBound) * 0.5f;\n\n        // If few enough triangles or too small, make this a leaf\n        if (indices.size() <= MAX_OCTREE_TRIS ||\n            (maxBound - minBound).norm() < MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Subdivide into 8 children\n        Vec3 childHalfSize = halfExtent * 0.5f;\n        std::vector<size_t> childIndices[8];\n\n        for (size_t idx : indices) {\n            const Triangle& tri = (*allTriangles)[idx];\n\n            // Check which children this triangle overlaps\n            for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n                Vec3 childCenter = center;\n                childCenter.x += (i & 1) ? childHalfSize.x : -childHalfSize.x;\n                childCenter.y += (i & 2) ? childHalfSize.y : -childHalfSize.y;\n                childCenter.z += (i & 4) ? childHalfSize.z : -childHalfSize.z;\n\n                if (triangleBoxOverlap(childCenter, childHalfSize, tri)) {\n                    childIndices[i].push_back(idx);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check if we can't split further (all triangles in one child)\n        bool canSplit = false;\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (!childIndices[i].empty() && childIndices[i].size() < indices.size()) {\n                canSplit = true;\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (!canSplit) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Build children\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (!childIndices[i].empty()) {\n                Vec3 childMin = center;\n                Vec3 childMax = center;\n                childMin.x = (i & 1) ? center.x : minBound.x;\n                childMax.x = (i & 1) ? maxBound.x : center.x;\n                childMin.y = (i & 2) ? center.y : minBound.y;\n                childMax.y = (i & 2) ? maxBound.y : center.y;\n                childMin.z = (i & 4) ? center.z : minBound.z;\n                childMax.z = (i & 4) ? maxBound.z : center.z;\n\n                children[i] = std::make_unique<Octree>();\n                children[i]->allTriangles = allTriangles;\n                children[i]->buildNode(childIndices[i], childMin, childMax);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\npublic:\n    // Check if a ray intersects this node's bounding box\n    bool rayIntersectsBox(const Vec3& p1, const Vec3& p2) const {\n        Vec3 d = (p2 - p1) * 0.5f;\n        Vec3 c = p1 + d - center;\n        Vec3 ad = {std::abs(d.x), std::abs(d.y), std::abs(d.z)};\n\n        if (std::abs(c.x) > halfExtent.x + ad.x) return false;\n        if (std::abs(c.y) > halfExtent.y + ad.y) return false;\n        if (std::abs(c.z) > halfExtent.z + ad.z) return false;\n\n        if (std::abs(d.y * c.z - d.z * c.y) > halfExtent.y * ad.z + halfExtent.z * ad.y + EPSILON) return false;\n        if (std::abs(d.z * c.x - d.x * c.z) > halfExtent.z * ad.x + halfExtent.x * ad.z + EPSILON) return false;\n        if (std::abs(d.x * c.y - d.y * c.x) > halfExtent.x * ad.y + halfExtent.y * ad.x + EPSILON) return false;\n\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Apply a function to all triangles potentially intersecting the ray\n    // Returns true if the function returns true for any triangle\n    template<typename Func>\n    bool applyToTris(const Vec3& p1, const Vec3& p2, Func&& func) const {\n        // If leaf node, check triangles directly\n      }\n\n        // Otherwise, descend to children\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (children[i] && children[i]->rayIntersectsBox(p1, p2)) {\n                if (children[i]->applyToTris(p1, p2, func)) return true;\n            }\n        }\n        return false;\n    }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Mesh Generation: Icosphere\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Generate an icosphere by subdividing an icosahedron\nclass IcosphereMesh {\npublic:\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n\n    IcosphereMesh(int subdivisions, val_t radius) {\n        // Initial icosahedron vertices\n        const val_t t = (1.0f + std::sqrt(5.0f)) / 2.0f;\n\n        std::vector<Vec3> vertices = {\n            Vec3(-1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0,  1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1, -t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0,  1, -t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( t,  0, -1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( t,  0,  1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-t,  0, -1).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-t,  0,  1).normalized() * radius\n        };\n\n        // Initial icosahedron faces (20 triangles)\n        std::vector<std::array<idx_t, 3>> faces = {\n            {0, 11, 5}, {0, 5, 1}, {0, 1, 7}, {0, 7, 10}, {0, 10, 11},\n            {1, 5, 9}, {5, 11, 4}, {11, 10, 2}, {10, 7, 6}, {7, 1, 8},\n            {3, 9, 4}, {3, 4, 2}, {3, 2, 6}, {3, 6, 8}, {3, 8, 9},\n            {4, 9, 5}, {2, 4, 11}, {6, 2, 10}, {8, 6, 7}, {9, 8, 1}\n        };\n\n        // Subdivide\n        for (int i = 0; i < subdivisions; ++i) {\n            std::vector<std::array<idx_t, 3>> newFaces;\n            std::map<std::pair<idx_t, idx_t>, idx_t> midpointCache;\n\n            auto getMidpoint = [&](idx_t i1, idx_t i2) -> idx_t {\n                auto key = std::make_pair(std::min(i1, i2), std::max(i1, i2));\n                auto it = midpointCache.find(key);\n                if (it != midpointCache.end()) return it->second;\n\n                Vec3 mid = (vertices[i1] + vertices[i2]) / 2.0f;\n                mid = mid.normalized() * radius;\n                idx_t idx = static_cast<idx_t>(vertices.size());\n                vertices.push_back(mid);\n                midpointCache[key] = idx;\n                return idx;\n            };\n\n            for (const auto& face : faces) {\n                idx_t a = getMidpoint(face[0], face[1]);\n                idx_t b = getMidpoint(face[1], face[2]);\n                idx_t c = getMidpoint(face[2], face[0]);\n\n                newFaces.push_back({face[0], a, c});\n                newFaces.push_back({face[1], b, a});\n                newFaces.push_back({face[2], c, b});\n                newFaces.push_back({a, b, c});\n            }\n            faces = std::move(newFaces);\n        }\n\n        // Build triangles (normals pointing inward for a \"room\")\n        triangles.reserve(faces.size());\n        for (const auto& face : faces) {\n            // Reverse winding to make normals point inward\n            triangles.emplace_back(vertices[face[2]], vertices[face[1]], vertices[face[0]]);\n        }\n    }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Random Number Generation\n// ============================================================================\n\nclass RandomGenerator {\n    std::mt19937 rng;\n    std::uniform_real_distribution<val_t> dist;\npublic:\n    explicit RandomGenerator(uint32_t seed = 42) : rng(seed), dist(0.0f, 1.0f) {}\n    val_t rand() { return dist(rng); }\n};\n\n// Generate a random point inside a triangle using barycentric coordinates\nVec3 randomPointInTriangle(const Triangle& t, RandomGenerator& rng) {\n    val_t u = rng.rand();\n    val_t v = rng.rand();\n    if (u + v > 1.0f) {\n        u = 1.0f - u;\n        v = 1.0f - v;\n    }\n    Vec3 ab = t.b - t.a;\n    Vec3 ac = t.c - t.a;\n    return t.a + ab * u + ac * v;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Ray-Triangle Intersection (Möller-Trumbore algorithm)\n// ============================================================================\n\nval_t rayTriangleIntersect(const Vec3& orig, const Vec3& dir,\n                            const Vec3& v0, const Vec3& v1, const Vec3& v2) {\n    Vec3 e1 = v1 - v0;\n    Vec3 e2 = v2 - v0;\n    Vec3 pvec = dir.cross(e2);\n    val_t det = e1.dot(pvec);\n\n    if (std::abs(det) < EPSILON) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    val_t invDet = 1.0f / det;\n    Vec3 tvec = orig - v0;\n    val_t u = tvec.dot(pvec) * invDet;\n    if (u < 0.0f || u > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    Vec3 qvec = tvec.cross(e1);\n    val_t v = dir.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n    if (v < 0.0f || u + v > 1.0f) return std::numeric_limits<val_t>::max();\n\n    return e2.dot(qvec) * invDet;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Visibility Testing (Octree-accelerated)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Check if a ray between two triangles is blocked by any other triangle\n// Uses octree for O(log N) instead of O(N) search\nbool isRayBlocked(const Vec3& from, const Vec3& to,\n                  const Octree& octree,\n                  size_t srcTriIdx, size_t dstTriIdx) {\n    Vec3 dir = to - from;\n    val_t rayLen = dir.norm();\n    if (rayLen < EPSILON) return true;\n    Vec3 dirNorm = dir / rayLen;\n\n    return octree.applyToTris(from, to, [&](size_t idx, const Triangle& tri) {\n        if (idx == srcTriIdx || idx == dstTriIdx) return false;\n\n        val_t dist = rayTriangleIntersect(from, dirNorm, tri.a, tri.b, tri.c);\n        if (dist > EPSILON && dist < rayLen - EPSILON) {\n            return true;  // Ray is blocked\n        }\n        return false;\n    });\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Form Factor Computation (Kij)\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Compute the cosine of angle between vector and triangle normal\nval_t cosPhi(const Vec3& v, const Vec3& normal) {\n    val_t vNorm = v.norm();\n    if (vNorm <= EPSILON) return ZERO;\n    return std::max(ZERO, v.dot(normal) / vNorm);\n}\n\n// Compute form factor Kij between triangle i (receiver) and triangle j (emitter)\nval_t computeKij(size_t idxI, size_t idxJ,\n                  const std::vector<Triangle>& triangles,\n                  const Octree& octree,\n                  RandomGenerator& rng) {\n    const Triangle& triI = triangles[idxI];\n    const Triangle& triJ = triangles[idxJ];\n\n    // Cull triangles facing the same direction\n    if (triI.normal().dot(triJ.normal()) > 0.99f) return ZERO;\n\n    val_t kij = ZERO;\n\n    for (int r = 0; r < NUM_RAYS; ++r) {\n        Vec3 pI = randomPointInTriangle(triI, rng);\n        Vec3 pJ = randomPointInTriangle(triJ, rng);\n\n        if (isRayBlocked(pI, pJ, octree, idxI, idxJ)) continue;\n\n        Vec3 v = pJ - pI;\n        val_t distSqr = v.squaredNorm();\n        if (distSqr < EPSILON) continue;\n\n        val_t cosPhiI = cosPhi(v, triI.normal());\n        val_t cosPhiJ = cosPhi(-v, triJ.normal());\n\n        if (cosPhiI <= ZERO || cosPhiJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n        kij += (cosPhiI * cosPhiJ) / (PI * distSqr);\n    }\n\n    return kij * INV_NUM_RAYS;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Tau (time delay) Computation\n// ============================================================================\n\nint computeTau(const Triangle& triI, const Triangle& triJ) {\n    val_t dist = (triI.center() - triJ.center()).norm();\n    return static_cast<int>(std::ceil(dist * INV_WAVE_SPEED));\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Room Response Simulation State\n// ============================================================================\n\nstruct SimulationState {\n    size_t numTriangles;\n    size_t numTimesteps;\n\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n    std::vector<val_t> areas;       // Area of each triangle\n    std::vector<val_t> rho;         // Reflectivity (0.0 to 1.0)\n    std::vector<val_t> kij;         // Form factors (N x N matrix, row-major)\n    std::vector<int> tau;           // Time delays (N x N matrix, row-major)\n    std::vector<val_t> radE;        // Emission radiosity (T x N matrix)\n    std::vector<val_t> radB;        // Reflected radiosity (T x N matrix)\n    std::vector<val_t> distances;   // Computed distances from source\n\n    Octree octree;                  // Spatial acceleration structure\n\n    size_t sourceIndex;\n\n    size_t idx2d(size_t i, size_t j) const { return i * numTriangles + j; }\n    size_t idxTN(size_t t, size_t n) const { return t * numTriangles + n; }\n};\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Initialization\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid initializeSimulation(SimulationState& state, int subdivisions, size_t timesteps,\n                          size_t sourceIdx, val_t reflectivity) {\n    // Generate mesh\n    IcosphereMesh mesh(subdivisions, 10.0f);  // Radius 10 units\n    state.triangles = std::move(mesh.triangles);\n    state.numTriangles = state.triangles.size();\n    state.numTimesteps = timesteps;\n    state.sourceIndex = sourceIdx % state.numTriangles;\n\n    printf(\"Generated icosphere mesh with %zu triangles\\n\", state.numTriangles);\n\n    // Build octree for spatial acceleration\n    printf(\"Building octree...\\n\");\n    state.octree.build(state.triangles);\n\n    // Initialize areas\n    state.areas.resize(state.numTriangles);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        state.areas[i] = state.triangles[i].area();\n    }\n\n    // Initialize reflectivity\n    state.rho.resize(state.numTriangles, reflectivity);\n\n    // Initialize matrices\n    state.kij.resize(state.numTriangles * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.tau.resize(state.numTriangles * state.numTriangles, 0);\n    state.radE.resize(timesteps * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.radB.resize(timesteps * state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n    state.distances.resize(state.numTriangles, ZERO);\n\n    // Set source emission (active for first half of timesteps)\n    size_t timeOn = 0;\n    size_t timeOff = timesteps / 2;\n    for (size_t t = timeOn; t < timeOff; ++t) {\n        state.radE[state.idxTN(t, state.sourceIndex)] = 1.0f;\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Precomputation Phase\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid computeFormFactors(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Computing form factors (Kij)...\\n\");\n    RandomGenerator rng(42);\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n            if (i == j) continue;\n            state.kij[state.idx2d(i, j)] = computeKij(\n                i, j, state.triangles, state.octree, rng);\n        }\n        if ((i + 1) % 100 == 0 || i + 1 == state.numTriangles) {\n            printf(\"  Progress: %zu/%zu triangles\\n\", i + 1, state.numTriangles);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nvoid computeTimeDelays(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Computing time delays (Tau)...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n            if (i == j) continue;\n            state.tau[state.idx2d(i, j)] = computeTau(\n                state.triangles[i], state.triangles[j]);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Simulation Phase (Wave Propagation)\n// ============================================================================\n\nvoid runSimulation(SimulationState& state) {\n    printf(\"Running wave propagation simulation...\\n\");\n\n    for (size_t t = 0; t < state.numTimesteps; ++t) {\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < state.numTriangles; ++i) {\n            val_t sumB = ZERO;\n\n            for (size_t j = 0; j < state.numTriangles; ++j) {\n                if (i == j) continue;\n\n                int tauij = state.tau[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n\n                // Skip if wave hasn't yet propagated from j to i\n                if (static_cast<int>(t) < tauij) continue;\n\n                val_t kij = state.kij[state.idx2d(i, j)];\n                if (kij <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Get radiosity from source triangle at time when emission occurred\n                size_t srcTime = t - static_cast<size_t>(tauij);\n                val_t radJ = state.radB[state.idxTN(srcTime, j)];\n                if (radJ <= ZERO) continue;\n\n                // Accumulate contribution: form factor * area * source radiosity\n                sumB += std::min(kij * state.areas[j], ONE) * radJ;\n            }\n\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792952359046,"sessionID":"ses_e8bb72d8bffeNsitue3vmWZC41","part":{"id":"prt_17448ed24001lqFs16ee0hBlxG","messageID":"msg_17448e92e001wzaZD3czcrhiC4","sessionID":"ses_e8bb72d8bffeNsitue3vmWZC41","type":"reasoning","text":"That output.txt is just an old session log, not critical to check. I'm now mapping out which parts of the computation can be parallelized - the octree build can stay sequential since it's small, while computeTimeDelays is trivially parallel since each iteration is independent.\n\nFor computeFormFactors, the tricky part is that the RNG is shared sequentially across all (i,j) pairs, and preserving the exact output hash means I need to preserve that exact sequence. Since culled pairs skip RNG draws entirely while non-culled pairs consume a fixed number of random calls, I'm thinking I could precompute each pair's RNG offset in a cheap preliminary pass over normal dot products, then jump each thread's RNG ahead using discard() before processing its assigned pairs in parallel.\n\nBut doing the math, discarding that many random draws per row turns out to cost roughly as much as just running everything sequentially, since mt19937's discard is a linear loop with no real jump-ahead optimization -- so this approach wouldn't actually save time despite preserving correctness.\n\nThat scales poorly though, quadratic in thread count for large core counts. A better idea might be a counter-based RNG where each pair's 64 draws can be addressed directly by index, avoiding sequential discarding altogether.\n\nBut changing the RNG entirely would alter the output stream and hash, which likely breaks the equivalence requirement since the grader probably checks against the original hash. Jump-ahead for mt19937 is theoretically possible via linear algebra over GF(2) but too complex to implement here, so I need to weigh whether the discard cost is actually significant relative to the expensive octree ray casting per pair.\n\nJump-ahead generators aren't available, so parallelizing the sequential RNG stream isn't straightforward. I'm considering just precomputing the entire sequence into a buffer upfront—for N=320 that's about 26MB of floats, which seems manageable.\n\nBut for larger N like 1280 or 5120, memory balloons to hundreds of MB or several GB, which is risky. I'm thinking instead about generating the stream in batches: process rows in chunks sized to fit a reasonable buffer (say 64MB), generating each chunk's draws sequentially and cheaply, since ray casting work per pair dominates runtime anyway and sequential draw generation is comparatively fast.\n\nComparing costs more carefully: generating the random draws needed per ray (4 draws, ~3-5ns each) is on the order of 20ns, while each ray's octree traversal and Möller-Trumbore intersection test likely costs 100-300ns. So across a pair with 16 rays, generation totals roughly 200ns versus ~3.2µs of compute — meaning sequential generation is only about 6% of total work, which keeps the sequential bottleneck from Amdahl's law fairly small.\n\nWith 256 cores that 6% sequential fraction would still cap scalability to around 16x, so I'm considering whether a hybrid scheme — sequentially filling a buffer per block, then parallelizing compute across blocks — is the most practical balance, since generating the whole stream at once or discarding to an offset doesn't really change the fundamental sequential cost.\n\nSince offsets are deterministic (64 floats per non-culled pair in sequence), each pair's thread can just read its 64-float slice in exact order and replay the same random-point-in-triangle logic. I could even skip blocking and generate the whole matrix sequentially first if memory allows, but I'll keep the row-block approach for scalability.\n\nFor N=320, the full buffer at 6.5M floats fits in one block, making generation fully sequential before parallel compute kicks in — roughly 20ms, negligible against total runtime. I considered parallelizing generation itself or overlapping block generation with compute, but discarding draws per-thread to skip ahead scales badly (O(offset) per thread), so I'll just accept the simple sequential generation step.\n\nSince each (i,j) pair writes to its own element, there's no race condition to worry about. For progress reporting, since parallel execution breaks the original sequential ordering, I'll print progress from the main thread after each block completes, trying to align block boundaries with multiples of 100 rows so the \"Progress: k/N\" lines land naturally.\n\nWork distribution across rows will be uneven since culled counts differ, so I should use dynamic or guided scheduling rather than static. Next I need to think through the time-stepping loop for runSimulation, where each timestep reads radiation values from earlier source times, and I need to be careful about whether tau can be zero.\n\nSince tau is computed from distance between triangle centers, it should be at least 1 for distinct triangles on an icosphere, but I want to reason more carefully about whether coincident centers could ever occur in that geometry, since a zero-delay case would create a race condition under parallelization that the original sequential version handled cleanly through ordering and the fact that radB starts at zero.\n\nI'll add a safety check: compute the minimum tau across all pairs, and if any i≠j pair yields tau==0, fall back to running the original sequential loop to preserve exact semantics — this costs little and makes the parallel path provably safe otherwise. Given the mesh sizes involved, the per-timestep work scales well when parallelized over triangles, since each (t,i) update only needs an independent inner loop over j.\n\nI should parallelize the i-loop inside each timestep using OpenMP with a static schedule, accepting a barrier per timestep since the overhead across all timesteps is negligible. Memory access per i involves gathering from a time-shifted row indexed by each triangle's own lag, which is unavoidable, so I'll leave that as-is. It's important I preserve the exact ascending-j summation order per i so floating-point results match bit-for-bit, and I need to watch out for GCC's fused multiply-add contraction under aggressive optimization flags, since that could silently change results.\n\nI'm checking that other parts of the pipeline — distance computation, form-factor calculation, octree traversal, and mesh initialization — are either naturally thread-safe or cheap enough that they don't need parallelizing, since octree traversal is read-only and the sequential build cost is negligible.\n\nFor validation, I'll keep things conservative: only parallelize the integer nonZeroKij count with a reduction since that's exact regardless of order, but leave distance min/max/sum sequential to avoid changing the printed floating-point average. The hash computation uses XOR, which is commutative, so I'm checking whether order-independence holds there too.\n\nI'll leave print_results untouched since it's outside the timed region, and I'll avoid printing extra diagnostic lines like thread counts since that could break output parsing. For the build, I'm wiring up CMake to require OpenMP and link the imported OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX target.\n\nI won't add an unconditional `#include <omp.h>` since nothing in the code actually calls omp runtime functions -- relying purely on pragmas is sufficient since CMake already enforces OpenMP support, and target_link_libraries and the executable name stay as they are.\n\nFor the RNG replication, I need to draw values from the same RandomGenerator (seeded 42) in identical order so buffered floats match the original exactly. The cull test between triangle normals is deterministic and independent of the random draws, so I can precompute per-pair draw counts: 64 draws for each ordered pair (i,j) where i≠j and the pair isn't culled, zero otherwise, which lets me correctly size and offset each block's buffer.\n\nNow I'm sketching the structure of computeFormFactors — setting up block-based processing where I generate the random draw sequence serially into a buffer matching the original ray loop, then compute per-pair offsets into that buffer so each pair's 64 draws (2 points × 2 draws × 16 rays) can be consumed in parallel while preserving the exact serial RNG order.\n\nTo make this parallelizable, each row's starting offset depends on a running prefix of non-culled pair counts, so I need a cheap pre-pass computing cull counts per row (parallelized) then a sequential prefix sum across rows, followed by sizing each processing block so its cumulative draw count stays under the memory cap before generating that block's random values.\n\nBuilding the block boundaries...\n\nThe RNG stream order matches the original exactly, so correctness holds; for N=320 the total draws come out to about 6.5M, generated sequentially in blocks of roughly 10-20ms each.\n\nI'm now parallelizing the row loop with dynamic scheduling since row costs vary, pulling each row's precomputed draws from the buffer and advancing a cursor per pairwise computation, while making sure the culling check exactly mirrors the one inside computeKij to avoid mismatches.\n\nWriting the draws-based kernel...\n\nI'm refactoring so both the random and deterministic sampling paths share a common pointInTriangleUV helper, keeping the original RandomGenerator-based computeKij intact while adding the new draw-driven variant.\n\nNow I'm adding a pre-pass to count, per row, how many non-culled pairs each index has, computing row offsets in parallel before the main fill.\n\nI want to verify the numeric accumulation for kij stays bit-identical to the original formula, since division rules out any FMA fusion risk. Now I'm checking whether runSimulation's parallelization condition correctly verifies that all tau values across i,j pairs are at least 1 before enabling the row-parallel path.\n\nThe parallel-over-i approach is only exact when every cross-term read at timestep t pulls from a strictly earlier timestep, so I need to confirm tau is never zero or negative — if tau hits zero there's a same-timestep dependency that forces the sequential path instead. I'll structure this as a shared update lambda invoked either under a parallel loop or a plain serial loop depending on that safety check, avoiding duplicated logic, and confirm that the writes to distinct row indices for different i values don't share cache lines in a way that causes false sharing.\n\nI'm settling on static scheduling for the main update loop and the distance/delay computations since work per i is roughly uniform, and using OpenMP reductions for the nonzero-kij and received-energy counts, with unsigned loop indices working fine under modern OpenMP.\n\nFor the received-energy check I need to restructure the early-break logic since breaking out of the parallel loop itself isn't allowed, but breaking an inner sequential loop within each thread's iteration is fine—so I'll track a per-i boolean flag and increment the reduction counter after the inner loop completes. I'm also weighing whether to parallelize the initial zero-fill of the kij matrix for NUMA-aware first-touch, but that would require restructuring memory allocation, so I'll skip it as a minor gain and leave the octree build sequential too, given its relatively small cost at these problem sizes.\n\nBefore making any further edits, I want to establish a baseline by copying the original unmodified repo to a temp directory, building it there without OpenMP, and running it with a few representative configurations so I have reference output and timing to compare against once the parallelized version is ready.\n\n","time":{"start":1792952298789,"end":1792952358923},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

To stay bit-identical while computing rows in\n    // parallel, the samples are generated sequentially in that same order into\n    // a bounded buffer, and rows are then evaluated concurrently from it.\n\n    // Exclusive prefix offsets (in samples) of each row within the global stream.\n    std::vector<size_t> rowOffset(N + 1, 0);\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        size_t count = 0;\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            if (i == j || isCulled(triangles[i], triangles[j])) continue;\n            ++count;\n        }\n        rowOffset[i + 1] = count * DRAWS_PER_PAIR;\n    }\n    for (size_t i = 0;
